## Report and scope

Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1203

Improve the reported warning-close then already-terminal refusal sequence with an executable recovery command. Existing warn/require policy and atomic structured close evidence are shipped contracts; preserve them. A normal pm update can append missing expected_result and actual_result while keeping the item terminal. Do not imply that force, reopen, or rewriting the original close event is required.

## Reported reproduction

## Summary

`pm close` accepts a close that it simultaneously reports as incomplete, and the obvious next command — re-running `close` with the flags the warning names — is rejected. The warning therefore steers an agent into a blocked retry.

## Reproduction

```
$ pm close pm-linear-tfj7 --author pi-orchestrator --resolution "..."
close_reason: "..."
warnings:
  - "close_validation_missing_fields:pm-linear-tfj7:expected_result (--expected-result),actual_result (--actual-result)"
```

The item is now closed, and the warning names two flags of `pm close`. Supplying them:

```
$ pm close pm-linear-tfj7 --author pi-orchestrator \
    --resolution "..." --expected-result "..." --actual-result "..."
Error: Command failed
What happened:
  Item pm-linear-tfj7 is already terminal; use --force to close again.
```

The only advertised way forward is `--force`, which reads as an override for re-closing a settled item — not as the way to finish a record the CLI just told you was unfinished.

`pm update` does work and is the correct path, but nothing in either message points to it:

```
$ pm update pm-linear-tfj7 --author pi-orchestrator --expected-result "..." --actual-result "..."
status: "closed"
changed_field_count: 2
```

## Why this matters for agents

The warning is well-formed and machine-readable, so an agent will act on it, and the action it implies is the one operation that is refused. The three plausible agent responses are all wrong: retry `close` (rejected), add `--force` (a destructive-sounding escape hatch used for a non-destructive completion), or ignore the warning (leaves the acceptance evidence the governance policy asked for permanently missing).

## Expected

Either:

1. `close` completes the record when it is re-run on a terminal item with only the missing fields — no `--force`, since nothing is being overwritten; or
2. the warning names the command that actually works, e.g. `pm update <id> --expected-result … --actual-result …`; or
3. the close is refused up front when `governance.require_close_reason`-style validation is unmet, rather than succeeding and reporting the gap afterwards.

Option 3 is the most consistent with how `require_close_reason` itself behaves — that one *does* fail closed:

```
Error: Close reason text is required because governance.require_close_reason is enabled
```

Two adjacent close-validation rules currently fail in opposite directions: one blocks the close, the other lets it through with a warning that cannot then be acted on.

## Environment

@unbrained/pm-cli 2026.9.5, Linux, Node 22.

## Delivery boundary

Intake only in PR #1204. This item remains open and unclaimed; no implementation or reproduction success is asserted. Implement through the public SDK with thin CLI adapters and executable negative controls before closing.
